proposal.rationale: Best RMSE so far was at 15 uL/s; removing mixing cycles should reduce foam that likely caused the E-217 fluid-detection failures at 20 uL/s.
proposal.diagnosis: The E-217 errors at 20 uL/s (three consecutive failures across tip retries/replacements) indicate the fault lies with the sample's foam, not tip or pickup issues. Post-dispense mixing at 2 cycles agitates the viscous BSA solution enough to create persistent foam, destabilizing the liquid-level sensor's surface detection. Since 15 uL/s with mixing=2 succeeded mechanically (RMSE 0.24) but 20 uL/s failed identically three times, foam buildup from mixing is the likely culprit rather than flow rate alone. Disabling mixing while staying at a low, previously-successful flow rate should avoid triggering the sensor fault while we continue tuning for RMSE accuracy.

payload.text: The error is caused by bubbles in the liquid. Move to clean wells and reduce mixing cycles to 1 or 0.

proposal.rationale: Reviewer identified mixing-induced bubbles as the cause of E-217 sensor failures; reducing mixing cycles to 1 should eliminate foam interference while retesting the flow rate (15 uL/s) that previously gave the best RMSE (0.24) among successful transfers.
proposal.diagnosis: Prior E-217 errors were caused by excessive mixing cycles (2) whipping the viscous BSA solution into foam/bubbles, which the liquid-level sensor could not read as a stable surface. Reducing mixing cycles to 1 and moving to fresh wells should avoid bubble formation while continuing the flow-rate sweep/refinement.
